main_text.head: I. Ex Ambrosio.
main_text.p: “S. Ambrosius in lib. de dignitate Sacerdotali cap.2. Honor (inquit) & sublimitas Episcopalis nullis poterit comparationibus adaequari; si Regum fulgori compares, & Principum diademati, longè erit inferius, quàm si plumbi metallum ad auri fulgorem compares: quippè cùm videas Regum colla & Principum submitti genibus Sacerdotum, & exof-culatis eorum dextris, orationibus eorum credant se com-muniri.” — Pag.40.

Cùm sæpe alibi, tùm præcipuè in hoc Tractatu Ambrosium Aduocatû accersis; semel, {d}Hinc S.Ambrosius in Epist. ad Theodosiû &c. Rursùs; {e}Vtinam habueremus plures Ambrosios,&c. Post, {f}Inter grauissimos Authores, praeexcellentia dignitatis Episcopalis supra Reges, habemus Ambrosium &c. Nec non, {g}Ambrosius diuino zelo accensus. Tandem, {h}Si multos haberemus Ambrosios.

Pontificij etiam alij omnes (quotis Papale fastigium suffulcire student) de Ambrosio omnia bona dicere, eius nomen decantare, dicta facta celebrare solet, quasi qui in uno Ambrosio (vtinam sano palato) ambrosiam ipsam degustâsse videantur. Quid rei sit auemus scire.

page.notes: Printed text is fully transcribed. Doubtful readings: "com-muniri" (the u may be read as a in print, so muniri is likely), "auemus" (kept as printed), "quotis" (as printed). The Greek asterisk mark before "Espencaeo" is treated as the reference mark for the note "Supra cap. 5." Chapter number in the running head reads "Cap.6." as printed. Small ornament at lower left is not text and is omitted.
